title: Midcycle burn tradeoff & runway sensitivity worksheet
body:
Purpose:
Quick working worksheet to surface non-linear tradeoffs between (A) headcount phasing, (B) slab vs burst capacity commitments, and (C) small price actions (per-token and embedding unit) in the next 6–12 months. Intended as a midcycle sanity check for execs and to feed into Q4 hiring gating rules.

Context & assumptions (baseline):
- Starting runway calc date: 2026-09-01 (this sheet rolled forward from Q2 forecast).
- Cash balance (net): $98.5M. Monthly non-G&A burn (hosting + COGS + direct ops): baseline $7.8M. G&A + R&D payroll burn: baseline $4.2M. Total monthly gross burn: $12.0M.
- ARR-like inflows: subscription & usage receipts monthly: currently averaging $4.1M recognized (net of credits).
- Net monthly burn (cash outflow after receipts) baseline: $7.9M.
- Token & infra assumptions (baseline unit economics): average hosted token cost to Redwood per 1k tokens = $0.0065 (weighted model mix), embedding unit (per 10k vectors compute equivalent) cost = $0.14.
- Hiring assumptions: average loaded cost per new IC hire = $18.5k/month (includes benefits & recruiting spread). Manager/lead average = $29k/month. Time-to-productivity ramp = 3 months at 60% cost efficiency, 6 months to 90%.
- Commitments: we have a 12-month Dedicated commitment with a 20% discount vs spot; current reserved utilization fringe = 65% leading to effective cost blending shown above.

Scenario definitions (fast labels):
1) Conservative hire freeze (Freeze) — hiring paused for 12 weeks except critical roles; no additional Dedicated commits; rely on spot burst when needed.
2) Incremental hire cadence (Moderate) — add 12 ICs over 3 months (4/month) plus 1 infra lead; maintain current Dedicated commit level.
3) Growth push (Aggressive) — add 30 ICs over 4 months, plus expand Dedicated by +25% capacity to secure predictability.
4) Price nudge (PriceUp) — implement a small per-token price increase of +6% tiered across mid-market customers (applied month 2) with a 2% expected churn.

Compressed results (6-month horizon, illustrative):
- Columns: scenario | incremental HC (FTE) | incremental monthly payroll delta | infra & commit delta | expected net burn change | runway months change (vs baseline 12.5 months)

ASCII table (rounded):
Scenario      | HC delta | Payroll delta | Infra delta | Net burn delta | Runway delta
--------------|----------|---------------|-------------|----------------|--------------
Baseline      | 0        | $0            | $0          | $0             | 0.0m
Freeze        | -6       | -$111k        | +$320k spot  | +$209k         | +0.4m
Moderate      | +12      | +$222k        | $0          | +$222k         | -0.3m
Aggressive    | +30      | +$555k        | +$480k commit| +$1.035M       | -1.3m
PriceUp       | 0        | $0            | -$120k perf  | -$120k (net)   | +0.2m

Notes on table:
- Payroll delta = incremental monthly loaded payroll cost. Negative numbers indicate savings.
- Infra delta: "+" indicates additional monthly cash outlay for capacity commitments or spot burst (e.g., Freeze sees higher spot). Commit delta for Aggressive includes monthly amortized uplift for extra Dedicated capacity purchase.
- Net burn delta simplifies offsetting revenue: PriceUp assumes +6% price yields +$110k/mo revenue but +2% churn reduces $230k/mo on mid-market book — net -$120k.

Detailed sensitivity (selected levers):
A) Price elasticity sweep (applied to mid-market cohort only, ~35% of receipts):
- +3% price → revenue +$55k/mo, churn 0.9% → revenue lost $103k/mo → net -$48k/mo (improves runway ~+0.08m)
- +6% price → net -$120k/mo (see PriceUp)
- +10% price → net -$310k/mo (churn accelerates to 6%, risky)

B) Dedicated commitment vs spot mix (utilization sensitivity):
- Each 5% increase in reserved utilization reduces per-1k token cost by ~0.0004 (so $0.06 per 100k tokens saved at scale), but requires committed cash.
- If utilization drops <55%, blended per-1k cost rises sharply; for our Q3 distribution a drop to 50% adds ~$360k/M of infra cash delta (modeled).

C) Hiring ramp risk: 3-month ramp means early months of hires worsen burn w/o commensurate revenue; break-even of an IC hire (on cost alone) requires incremental revenue or infra savings of ~$20k/month sustained.

Actionable experiments to run (quick):
- EPIC-Runway-Sweep (owner: Ethan) — 2-week model recalibration: pull last 12 months token mix, recalc weighted per-token cost via infra telemetry. (JIRA-FIN-2143)
- Price microtest (owner: Nalini) — run +3% A/B on 15% of mid-market customers for 4 weeks; measure elasticity signals (acceptance, usage, churn intent).
- HC gating rule (owner: Priya) — require product/eng signoff with a 6-week rolling token cost delta < 3% for any hiring >5 ICs/month.

Open questions / discussion points:
- Committed vs burst trade: can SRE/infra reduce spot reliance by shifting low-utilization regional pools into short-term commitments with cheaper break clauses? Legal review needed.
- Can we target cost-of-infra payback by selective model-quantization push (engineering asks for 8 weeks to prototype savings)? Estimated upside: 6–12% token-cost reduction.
- How correlated is churn to small price increases for customers using Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted API? Hypothesis: Dedicated customers are less price-sensitive, but bigger ARR exposures (one customer leaving is larger). Need cohort split.

Appendix (quick calcs):
- Baseline runway months = cash / net monthly burn = $98.5M / $7.9M ≈ 12.47 months.
- Add Aggressive net burn +$1.035M → new burn = $8.935M → runway ≈ 11.0 months (delta -1.47). Table rounded -1.3m.
- Break-even price increase: given churn sensitivity, small price moves (+1–4%) likely beneficial; >6% requires careful cohort segmentation.

Decision record (proposed):
- Short-term (30 days): approve Price microtest (+3%) on 15% mid-market (Nalini), pause non-critical hiring for 6 weeks (Priya), prioritize infra telemetry pull (Ethan).
- Medium-term (3 months): reconvene with SRE/product on quantization pilot; if pilot predicts >6% token-cost reduction, plan a targeted Dedicated expansion instead of hiring surge.

Notes to self (work-in-progress):
- This is intentionally compact — follow-on sheet will be a tabbed workbook with month-by-month cashflow, cohort churn table, and per-route token mix.
- TODO: attach the last 6 weeks of Stripe receipts + reserved usage CSV for proper validation.

Edits: 2026-10-04 — updated PriceUp churn assumption after Nalini's early cohort feedback (churn moved from 3% → 2% mid-market)
